records.Concise description: The de facto legacy protocol used by Bitcoin ASIC miners to receive pool jobs and submit proof-of-work shares.
records.Deeper researched summary: Stratum V1 was introduced by the Slush/Braiins lineage in 2012 to replace less efficient pooled-mining approaches. In the common deployment model, the pool server constructs the block job and miners vary nonce/extranonce fields while submitting lower-difficulty shares as accounting proofs. The protocol is an application-layer mining coordination system; it is not part of Bitcoin consensus, and its original transport does not provide Stratum V2’s authenticated encrypted Noise transport.
Creators / founders: Marek 'Slush' Palatinus — original Stratum mining-protocol creator in the Slush Pool lineage
records.Launch / history: Introduced in 2012 and remains widely deployed by Bitcoin pools and ASIC firmware in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is still the baseline miners encounter, making it essential for understanding shares, worker jobs, pool control of templates, and why later protocols target encryption and miner template choice.
Important technical or cultural characte: Legacy plaintext/unauthed transport unless separately wrapped

Official sources.label: Braiins — past and future of Bitcoin mining protocols

records.Verification basis: Braiins-controlled historical/technical materials plus continuing 2026 pool endpoint documentation verify both origin and current widespread use.
Research notes / uncertainties: Implementation details vary among pools and firmware; do not claim one vendor extension is universal Stratum V1 behavior.

records.Concise description: An open Bitcoin mining protocol suite adding authenticated encrypted transport, more efficient binary messaging, and optional miner-side job negotiation/declaration.
records.Deeper researched summary: Stratum V2 is a modular protocol family rather than one universally deployed feature. Its Mining Protocol handles channels/jobs/shares over authenticated encrypted transport; Job Declaration and Template Distribution components can let miners construct and declare transaction sets instead of accepting only pool-built templates. Active 2026 repositories and releases show continued implementation work and real deployments, but advanced components are not universally supported across pools or firmware.
Creators / founders: Matt Corallo — BetterHash concepts influenced the job-negotiation direction
records.Launch / history: Specification and implementation work began in 2019; production and beta deployments expanded through 2024–2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It addresses both transport security/efficiency and pool-template centralization, but only when the relevant optional components are actually deployed.
records.Verification basis: Current official specification and actively maintained 2026 open-source repositories verify protocol components and implementation maturity.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not claim universal pool, firmware, Job Declaration, or Template Distribution deployment.
Miner-side transaction selection requires the relevant components and deployment architecture; SV2 transport alone does not guarantee template choice.

records.Entity / project type: Bitcoin node mining RPC / BIP specification
records.Concise description: The deployed Bitcoin JSON-RPC template interface defined by BIP 22 and extended for pooled mining by BIP 23.
records.Deeper researched summary: BIP 22 replaced simplistic header-only work delivery with a full block-template interface that gives mining software transaction and block-construction data and allows defined customization. BIP 23 adds pooled-mining extensions such as mutations, submissions, and block proposals. Bitcoin Core continues implementing `getblocktemplate`. It is a mining API/RPC interface, not a Bitcoin consensus rule: any resulting block must still satisfy consensus validation.
records.Launch / history: BIP 22 and BIP 23 were assigned in February 2012 and remain deployed specifications implemented by Bitcoin Core.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is foundational plumbing between a validating node and mining/template software and influenced subsequent decentralized template-selection efforts.
Important technical or cultural characte: Full block-template data rather than simple getwork headers
records.Verification basis: Deployed BIP specifications and current Bitcoin Core source verify the interface and its continued implementation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply BIP 22/23 changes Bitcoin consensus; it specifies an API/RPC contract for constructing/proposing work.

records.Concise description: Matt Corallo’s 2018 proposal to shift Bitcoin block-template construction from pool operators toward individual miners, later superseded in practice by Stratum V2 work.
records.Deeper researched summary: BetterHash proposed separating share/payout coordination from transaction selection by letting individual miners build block templates and submit commitments to pools. It became influential design prior art but did not achieve broad production adoption as its own standard. The reference mining-proxy repository was archived in 2025, and Bitcoin Optech treats BetterHash as a predecessor that fed into Stratum V2’s job-negotiation direction.
records.Launch / history: Proposed in 2018; prototype/reference work followed, but the project never became a broadly deployed standalone mining standard and its repository is now archived.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It reframed pool centralization as separable from payout pooling and directly influenced modern miner-template negotiation designs.
Important technical or cultural characte: Historical design influence on Stratum V2
Proposal/implementation history, not current standalone deployment
records.Verification basis: Creator repository plus Bitcoin Optech historical context verify the proposal and its superseded/non-broadly-deployed status.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe BetterHash as a currently deployed pool protocol.
Its significance is design lineage, not current network share.
